title: api: app factory, deps, schemas, state/villages/admin routes
criteria:
Build the HTTP API (BUILD.md section 9, Phase 0 endpoints only) with FastAPI. All routes live under the prefix /api.
Endpoints: GET /api/state -> StateView; GET /api/meta; GET /api/villages/{id} -> VillageView; PATCH /api/villages/{id} body {name} -> VillageBrief; GET /api/villages/{id}/slots/{slot} -> SlotView; POST /api/villages/{id}/build body {slot, type} -> BuildQueueView; POST /api/admin/pause -> StateView; POST /api/admin/resume -> StateView; POST /api/admin/new-world body {seed:int|None, speed:int, player_name:str, tribe:str, bot_count:int} -> StateView.
Files: deps.py (get_session, get_cfg, get_world, get_now, get_player as in the spec), schemas.py (request bodies BuildBody, RenameBody, NewWorldBody), routes/state.py (state + meta), routes/villages.py, routes/admin.py, main.py with `create_app(serve_static: bool = True) -> FastAPI`.
Error handling: an exception handler turns services.errors.GameError into JSON {"error": {"code": code, "message": message}} with HTTP status NOT_FOUND->404, FORBIDDEN->403, WORLD_ENDED->409, every other code ->400. Request validation errors (422) may stay default.
Tests (tests/api/test_api_phase0.py) with fastapi.testclient.TestClient(create_app(serve_static=False)) and app.dependency_overrides[get_session] yielding the rollback-protected `s` fixture session from tests/conftest.py (so nothing is committed): POST /api/admin/new-world {seed:1, speed:1, player_name:'ผู้เล่น', tribe:'stonehold', bot_count:0} -> 200 with world info; GET /api/state -> 200 with player name, villages list of 1, paused false, speed 1, unread_reports 0; GET village -> 40 buildings, resources 750 each (right after creation, tolerate tiny float growth: use pytest.approx(750, abs=1)); POST build {slot:1,type:'woodcutter'} -> 200 BuildQueueView with slot 1; the same POST again -> 400 with error.code == 'QUEUE_FULL'; GET slots/1 -> current woodcutter; PATCH rename -> 200 and the new name appears in the next GET; build on an unknown village -> 404 NOT_FOUND; POST /api/admin/pause -> state.paused true; POST /api/admin/resume -> paused false; GET /api/meta has buildings (16), units (9), tribes (3 with name_th and description_th); mutating requests (build, rename, pause/resume; new-world is allowed) when the world has status 'ended' -> 409 WORLD_ENDED (set world.status='ended' directly in the DB inside the test); GET /api/state with no world at all -> 404 NOT_FOUND (delete or end worlds in the test first; note get_world returns the newest world of ANY status, so for the 404 case delete all World rows after clearing dependants, or run it on a fresh empty rollback session by deleting everything in FK order).
notes:
DESIGN (follow exactly):
- deps.get_session: generator `with session_scope() as s: yield s`. get_cfg: realm.core.config.load_config() (lru_cached). get_world(s): the world row with the highest id regardless of status (select(World).order_by(World.id.desc()).limit(1)); none -> GameError NOT_FOUND ('ไม่พบโลก'). get_now(world): worlds.world_now(world, datetime.now(timezone.utc)) (datetime.now is allowed in API deps). get_player(s, world): the single Player with is_bot False in that world; none -> NOT_FOUND. Add `require_running(world)` helper dependency raising GameError WORLD_ENDED ('โลกนี้จบแล้ว') when world.status != 'running'; use it on build, PATCH rename, pause, resume. new-world does NOT use it.
- All routes are plain `def` (sync) functions so FastAPI runs them in a threadpool with the sync session. Use `Depends`.
- GET /api/state: StateView(game_now=now, paused=world.paused_at is not None, speed, ends_at, world_id, player={'id','name','tribe'}, villages=[villages.village_brief(s, v, cfg) for the player's villages ordered by id], unread_reports=count of Report rows of this player with is_read false). (Reports table exists, will be empty.)
- GET /api/villages/{id}: villages.get_village_view(s, player.id, id, now, cfg). PATCH: villages.rename_village(...) then return villages.village_brief(s, village, cfg) (re-read the village with s.get(Village, id)). GET slots: villages.get_slot_view. POST build: villages.build(...) then return BuildQueueView built from the BuildQueue row (id, slot, type, target_level, finishes_at).
- admin: pause -> worlds.pause(s, datetime.now(timezone.utc)) then return the same StateView builder as /api/state; resume likewise. new-world: seed = body.seed or random.randrange(1, 2**31); worlds.create_world(s, seed=..., speed=..., player_name=..., tribe=..., bot_count=..., cfg=cfg, real_now=datetime.now(timezone.utc)); then return the StateView of the NEW world (build it with the same helper; helper signature e.g. build_state(s, world, cfg) living in routes/state.py and imported by admin.py). Note worlds.pause/resume use worlds.current_world (running worlds only), which is consistent because require_running guards them.
- GET /api/meta returns JSON: {'buildings': {key: {name_th, kind, max_level, capital_max_level, produces, fixed_slot}}, 'units': {key: {name_th, type, attack, def_inf, def_cav, speed, carry, upkeep}}, 'tribes': {key: {name_th, description_th}}, 'speeds': [1,3,5,10], 'slots': {'field': [1,18], 'center': [20,38]}} built from cfg (no hard-coded balance numbers).
- main.create_app: FastAPI(title='Realm of Villages'); include routers with prefix '/api'; register the GameError handler; if serve_static and the directory <repo>/web exists, mount it with StaticFiles(directory=..., html=True) at '/' AFTER the API routers (import StaticFiles from fastapi.staticfiles). Path to web/: Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / 'web'. Do NOT add websocket code (a later task adds /ws).
- The pydantic request body fields: BuildBody(slot: int, type: str); RenameBody(name: str); NewWorldBody(player_name: str, tribe: str, seed: int | None = None, speed: int = 1, bot_count: int = 30) — required fields before defaulted ones.
- Short correct Thai only; double-check tone marks.
